skill.name: remote-system-maintenance
skill.description: Guides diagnostics, cleanup, and documentation for remote Ubuntu and Debian systems over SSH or tmux sessions.
skill.summary: Run structured remote Linux diagnostics, cleanup, package maintenance, and session documentation.

content.value_statement: Remote Linux upkeep needs repeatable checks, careful cleanup, and clear records. This skill guides diagnostics, package maintenance, disk recovery, and post-maintenance documentation.
actual_capabilities: Outlines a three-phase workflow for diagnostics, log review, and package assessment.
Lists Ubuntu and Debian cleanup steps for apt, journals, snaps, and temporary directories.
Explains how to identify disabled snap revisions before removing them.
Defines session documentation requirements for system state, actions, and follow-up work.
Provides expected time and disk recovery ranges for maintenance sessions.
limitations: Does not connect to servers or execute commands by itself.
Focused on Ubuntu and Debian systems, not every Linux distribution.
Requires operator judgment before removing packages, logs, or temporary files.
Does not replace backups, change management, or incident response procedures.

use_cases.title: Pre-Window Server Checks
use_cases.description: System administrators can gather baseline resource, log, and package data before planned maintenance.

use_cases.title: Disk Recovery Sessions
use_cases.description: DevOps engineers can follow ordered cleanup steps to reclaim space on overloaded Ubuntu or Debian hosts.

use_cases.title: Maintenance Reporting
use_cases.description: Managed service providers can document actions, improvements, and follow-up recommendations after remote work.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Health Check
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the remote-system-maintenance skill to prepare a basic diagnostic checklist for an Ubuntu server. Include disk, memory, CPU, and service checks.

prompt_templates.title: Cleanup Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the remote-system-maintenance skill to create a cautious cleanup plan for a Debian host with low disk space. Include pre-checks and expected records.

prompt_templates.title: Package and Log Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the remote-system-maintenance skill to assess package upgrades, orphaned dependencies, journal usage, and disabled snap revisions for a remote server.

prompt_templates.title: Full Maintenance Runbook
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the remote-system-maintenance skill to build an end-to-end runbook for a remote Ubuntu maintenance window. Include diagnostics, cleanup, validation, and reporting.

output_examples.input: Request: Prepare a quick Ubuntu health check before cleanup.
output: Baseline checklist covering hostname, OS, kernel, disk use, memory, CPU, load, zombies, critical services, and recent system errors.
Operator record template for starting values and follow-up notes.

output_examples.input: Request: Plan disk recovery for a Debian server with low root volume space.
output_examples.output: A staged cleanup sequence for package lists, upgrades, unused dependencies, package cache, journal retention, snap revisions, and temporary directory review.

output_examples.input: Request: Summarize a completed maintenance session.
output_examples.output: A concise report with initial and final resource states, actions taken, quantified space recovered, remaining issues, and monitoring recommendations.

best_practices: Record baseline metrics before each maintenance action.
Review package and snap removal targets before confirming changes.
Capture final measurements and follow-up tasks after cleanup.
anti_patterns: Running cleanup commands without checking disk, package, and log state first.
Removing packages, snap revisions, or temporary files without verifying ownership and purpose.
Skipping session documentation after changes to a remote production host.

faq.question: Does this skill execute maintenance commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides structured guidance. The operator or agent must decide what to run and confirm changes.

faq.question: Which systems does it focus on?
faq.answer: It focuses on Ubuntu and Debian systems, especially remote hosts managed through SSH or tmux.

faq.question: Can it help recover disk space?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers package cache cleanup, journal pruning, disabled snap revisions, and temporary directory review.

faq.question: Does it include reporting guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It asks for system identification, before-and-after resource states, actions taken, and follow-up recommendations.

faq.question: Is it suitable for production servers?
faq.answer: It can support production maintenance when used with backups, approvals, and local change control.

faq.question: Can it diagnose security events?
faq.answer: It includes authentication and security event review, but it is not a full incident response playbook.
